priorityPolicy.rule: Repository, NEXUS, SPECTRA, release, toolchain and shared HALO architecture close before individual HALO feature optimization unless a feature defect blocks release correctness.

acceptance: Popup discovers paused and muted media tabs beyond the recent-activity window.
Discovery does not acquire the heavy Content Runtime merely to enumerate media tabs.
Service-worker restart reconstructs inventory from live documents.
Probe fan-out is bounded and receiver failures are isolated.
Unit and installed-browser evidence cover multiple tabs.
Only explicitly shipped ready or beta modules enter the production dynamic-import, transitive source-import and release payload graph.
Coming, disabled and unspecified modules may remain in source/catalog but are absent from the production ZIP unless explicitly admitted as non-executable catalog data.
Production source-graph and artifact tests prove excluded module code and dependencies are physically absent.
Every plugin has an explicit release stage; missing status cannot silently mean coming or shipped.
Source presence, catalog visibility, payload admission and runtime enablement are distinct generated facts.
Registry generation fails closed on ambiguous release state.
Web-accessible resources and runtime/content entry surfaces are generated from admitted capabilities.
Release build rejects broad orphan resource exposure, catalog-only transitive imports and source/projection drift.
Authoritative roadmap work has one machine-readable owner and cannot coexist with a misleading zero-backlog projection.
GitHub issue/project projections are derived or reconciled from that owner.
Every retained closure item has id, priority, owner, status and acceptance evidence requirements.
CI validates schema, unique ids, terminal evidence and the HALO feature P2 priority rule.
At least one stable independent replay lane executes repository code continuously and is expected green on main.
Exact-head local product evidence remains independent rather than being weakened or replaced.
tasks.blocker: GitHub-hosted jobs for the current private repository still terminate before Checkout with zero executable steps, so no hosted run can be represented as green until runner allocation is restored.

acceptance: The declared minimum Chrome version is exercised by a pinned browser lane, or the manifest floor is raised to the continuously proven version.
Current-Chrome and minimum-Chrome evidence are reported separately.
Exact-head evidence measures cold interactive latency, hotkey end-to-end latency and service-worker wake latency.
Long-task, CPU, heap/leak and tab/media-scale stress workloads have reproducible evidence before budgets are admitted.
Runtime SLO evidence is release-bound and distinct from bundle byte ceilings; hard budgets cannot be invented before at least two independent baseline runs.
Promotion to ready requires correctness, failure-boundary, lifecycle/restart, permission/privacy, accessibility, runtime resource, bundle and browser evidence.
Promotion is rejected mechanically when an applicable evidence owner is absent.
Unused direct dependencies are machine-detected and removed only with regenerated lock plus full build/test proof.
Current retained debt includes HALO file-saver, jszip, @types/file-saver and runtime-misclassified @types/qrcode; stale or newly introduced debt fails governance.
Dependency governance covers vulnerability, freshness, maintenance health, license, bundle contribution, direct-use classification and replacement value.
A clean advisory audit cannot be reported as complete dependency lifecycle health, and every executable lock domain is audited independently.
Automated update PRs exist for package dependencies and GitHub Actions pins.
Low-risk update promotion includes tests plus production artifact/performance deltas.
TypeScript 7 migration is evaluated as a dedicated compiler epoch rather than a blind dependency bump.
Diagnostics, typecheck, build, artifact and runtime comparisons are recorded before promotion.
Obsolete TypeScript 5 compatibility glue is removed only after the migration proves equivalence or improvement.
Direct dependency versions are revalidated against current stable upstream releases and repository compatibility.
Playwright, esbuild, Biome, Turbo, Terser, darkreader, jose and pinyin-pro are explicitly reconciled.
Root and nexus lock/resolution domains are either intentionally separate with independent frozen-install evidence or converged to one authority.
No unverified dependency universe exists outside CI/release ownership.
Third-party GitHub Actions are pinned to immutable commit SHAs.
Automated dependency ownership updates those SHAs without returning to mutable tags.
Each release emits a machine-readable SBOM and third-party license inventory bound to the exact artifact.
Build provenance/attestation binds source, builder/tool identity and resulting artifact digest.
Permission verification distinguishes declared-and-used from required-at-install.
SPECTRA required permissions and host scope have machine-readable least-privilege rationale or are moved to narrower optional/capability-bound admission.
Users can explicitly export a redacted bounded diagnostic bundle without default remote telemetry or a new always-on diagnostic background owner.
Bundle includes version/browser/permission/runtime identity and bounded non-PII state while proving URL/title/token/storage values cannot leak.
Critical Popup and SidePanel paths have automated keyboard, focus and accessible-name/state checks.
Zoom, reduced-motion and contrast-sensitive states have explicit acceptance evidence.
Critical UI states have deterministic visual capture owners pinned to browser, viewport, locale, theme and reduced-motion state; ordinary tests cannot overwrite baselines.
The policy remains baseline-required until pinned Chrome baselines are explicitly re-recorded and reviewed, after which exact SHA comparison may be enforced without invented fuzzy thresholds.
Property or mutation testing is applied selectively to parsers, protocol guards and state machines where it finds failures ordinary examples miss.
No global vanity coverage percentage substitutes for risk-owned evidence.
Large or high-risk activation/runtime closures cannot be promoted without focused behavior contracts.
Release tooling detects admitted high-risk modules that have no registered focused test owner.
Content execution requirements are generated from plugin capability metadata rather than parallel manual lists/imports.
Generator and transitive production source-graph drift fail repository verification.
Active service projection derives from owned lifecycle contracts rather than a manual storage-key/service list.
Every projected service has an owner, readiness semantics and disposer.
A Timer or Pomodoro feature cannot be promoted from catalog-only status until work expected to survive an unmounted SidePanel uses persisted deadline state plus Background/alarm ownership.
Any future promoted timer proves restart, duplicate/late alarm and completion side-effect idempotence before release admission.
Every requested split range is preserved in the user-visible result.
File/count/page/aggregate byte limits, cancellation and bounded execution prevent unbounded SidePanel memory/CPU use.
Heavy PDF work is isolated from the UI owner and has focused correctness/resource tests before ready promotion.
Remaining individual feature internals are audited only after shared release-admission, lifecycle, dependency and evidence gates are established.
Any promoted feature defect discovered earlier may preempt this order only when it blocks release correctness.
